headline: Peruvian Sol Closes at S/3.46 Against US Dollar Amid Copper Drop and US Caution
summary: The Peruvian sol closed at S/3.464 against the US dollar in interbank trading, ticking up roughly 0.06% amid falling copper prices and US election caution.
why: Peru is a leading global copper exporter, making its currency highly sensitive to international copper prices and global foreign exchange flows.
why_moved: The exchange rate adjusted slightly in response to lower global copper prices and cautious sentiment ahead of US political events.
